title: App
description: App pod health: replicas, restarts, OOMKilled, CPU and memory usage. App logs, traces and request metrics live in Sentry. See helm/README.md's Alloy section for how this data gets to Grafana Cloud. Use the Environment variable to pick production or development data.

panels.title: Service replicas
panels.description: Available app replicas right now (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available). The app is configured for 1 replica, so seeing a drop below that (0) means it's down - check the Events panel on the Kubernetes Cluster dashboard for why. If it's ever scaled beyond 1, this reflects that too, unlike a plain up/down flag.

panels.title: Container restarts
panels.description: App container restarts per 5m window, summed across all its pods - a proxy for crash-looping. The PodCrashLooping alert (terraform/alerting.tf) fires on a sustained elevated rate.

panels.title: Container OOMKilled
panels.description: Approximate OOM kill count of the app container over time (defaults to 0, jumping when its last crash is currently flagged OOMKilled). Not an exact historical tally - kube-state-metrics only exposes the current last-termination reason, not a per-event counter, so a restart for unrelated reasons followed by one OOM would show the full restart count here. The ContainerOomKilled alert (terraform/alerting.tf) fires on any occurrence.

targets.expr: sum by (container) ((kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="cpu", deployment_environment_name="$environment", container="app"} * 0) or (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{deployment_environment_name="$environment", container="app"} * on (namespace, pod, container) kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled", deployment_environment_name="$environment", container="app"}))

panels.title: Container CPU usage
panels.description: CPU usage as a percentage of the app container's own configured resources.limits.cpu (not the host's total CPU) - e.g. 50% means it's using half of what it's allowed. Above 100% isn't possible - the kernel throttles it at the limit instead.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (container) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{deployment_environment_name="$environment", container="app"}[5m])) / sum by (container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{deployment_environment_name="$environment", container="app", resource="cpu"})

panels.title: Container memory usage
panels.description: Working-set memory as a percentage of the app container's own configured resources.limits.memory (not the host's total memory) - e.g. 50% means it's using half of what it's allowed. Unlike CPU, exceeding this limit gets the container OOMKilled - see the Container OOMKilled panel.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{deployment_environment_name="$environment", container="app"}) / sum by (container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{deployment_environment_name="$environment", container="app", resource="memory"})
